issues.title: Tracker Ruptela Eco4 Light 3G parsing error with latesr server version
comments: Which version did it work on?
Also please provide the protocol documentation.

Hi,

I used to have traccar-windows-64-4.10

Hi,

This is the document of the protocol I have.

Thanks!
You can't email attachments to GitHub, if you didn't know. It doesn't work.
I don't have a Scribd subscription.
Why can't you just upload it here in GitHub?

Hi,

i have uploaded the fie
https://github.com/JavierCollazo/Files/blob/main/ruptela-protocol-v-1-113%2020220520.pdf
I have tried several server versions and the tracker works until v5.5.

Thanks!

Javier.
@jinzo it seems like one of your changes might have broken something. Can you please look into it.
I'm on vacations but will take a look in the next few days. Just noticed that it works until version 5.5 -> which probably predates my changes? Will investigate and report back.
@JavierCollazo just to be more clear. The latest version of tracker that works is v5.4 right? Do you have the setting 'Send Data without GPS' enabled in Ruptela settings by any chance?

Hi,

The trackers are working also in v5.5.

Yes, that option is activated (I don't know whether it is doing something
because when indoors I don't get map position)

When I updated the server, I updated the trackers also and activated that
option. Maybe too many changes at the same time.

I recall trying v5. 8 whithout that option and they did not work either.

Thanks.

Javier.

@JavierCollazo so the first version that is not working is v5.6? This really helps us to pinpoint the issue. The "Longitude out of range" message/exception was added around that time, so that could partially be a reason.

@tananaev a quick double check confirms that my first commits to Ruptela decoder were June 11th and 5.8 was released on May 31th. So none of the Ruptela changes I actually did made it into a release yet. I will still pursue this as I'm interested in what's happening - but I would guess that the older versions were happily storing invalid Positions and the Longitude out of range check is now triggering and highlighting this issue.

Off the top of my head the working theory now is that the device is trying to send a stored position with invalid Longitude (eg. no GPS data) and as it receives a negative response it does not try further. If I would be @JavierCollazo I would try to configure the device with "Send Data without GPS" turned off and 'delrecords' sms command to clear the stored records/positions.

As I was writing this, I remembered that I got a fancy .zip from Ruptela ppl, where they have a 'data parser' simple utility for checking. And inputting your hex I get a result (pasted below) that would confirm my suspicions. This packets have invalid Longitude and Latitude and the 'new' Longitude exception/check highlighted the issue. As not even Ruptela is handling this case (there is a big fat warning beside "Send Data without GPS" that this should not be used on Ruptela service) - the 'delrecords' and turning off this option should fix this and prevent it from happening in the future. 

@tananaev - do we wish to handle this in the parser itself? eg. discard positions with invalid longitude/latitude (so I would guess catching the exception and returning 'ok' response & tagging the position as invalid ?)
